newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch see new shortfall on social security funds.
newsitem.headline: Dutch see new shortfall on social security funds.

text.p: Dutch social security funds face a shortfall of some 4.5 billion guilders over the years 1996 and 1997, official sources said on Monday, confirming figures which appeared in Dutch media at the weekend.
"The figures which have been circulating in the media are more or less accurate," said one source.
The shortfall for the social security funds is about the same size as a windfall in 1996 tax revenues, over and above previous official estimates, announced in January.
Official sources declined to say whether the social security shortfall would have any implications for the Netherlands' compliance with EMU convergence criteria.
Earlier this month Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm told parliament the Netherlands was on target for an EMU public sector deficit of 1.9 percent of GDP in 1996.
This was after news of the higher than expected tax revenues for that year but before the latest news of a deterioration in the position of the social security funds.
